cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Not Dismissed
cards.instruction: Keep someone present by treating departure as a privilege only you can grant.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Before you put your coat on, I'd like to formally conclude our coffee.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I only stopped for ten minutes. My bus is due.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Then I'll consider an early departure. Sit down while I decide.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The café's closing. They've asked us both to leave.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. We'll wait outside together. Their permission to leave doesn't replace mine.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 claims control of concluding coffee, A3 considers early departure as a privilege, and A5 rejects venue permission as sufficient for leaving A.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 brief visit and bus cause A3 pending early departure; B4 cafe closure causes A5 moving the same controlled wait outside.

heightening.evidence: B4 requires physical exit, but A5 distinguishes leaving the venue from being released by A.

specificity.evidence: A1 coat and coffee, B2 bus and B4 closing cafe establish a clear social departure.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 their-permission-versus-mine distinction is earned by B4 demand affecting both characters.
